A separate block on hand signals and the dashboard
A pre-exam run-through mode on signs only
antiFeatures: Don't load sign images from a server at the moment of the question
Don't ask about a sign without the sign itself on screen
Don't mix signs from other countries with American ones
driving-test-prep-4.monetization: The reference and basic practice free, the full set of tests and the pre-exam mode for a one-time purchase around 4 dollars, cheap because of the narrow topic

driving-test-prep-5.title: The topics that fail people on the exam but get skipped by apps
driving-test-prep-5.oneLiner: A trainer on junior driver restrictions, fines, and alcohol that aren't in the usual apps but get asked constantly
driving-test-prep-5.gap: Apps drill signs and speed limits well, but whole layers of the exam are left out: junior driver and probationary period restrictions, fines and consequences for breaking them, calculating alcohol content, hand signals, when to turn headlights on. It's exactly these topics that fail people, because practice created a false sense of readiness. Nobody has assembled a targeted trainer on the topics that come up on the exam en masse but get systematically skipped.
mechanisms: The topics that fail people on the exam but get skipped by apps
Fines, restrictions, and alcohol calculation fall out of practice
Breaking down concrete scenarios is valued over cramming
driving-test-prep-5.pitch: A complementary trainer on the very topics that fail people: junior driver and probationary period restrictions, fines and consequences of violations, calculating allowable alcohol, hand signals, headlight rules. Each topic gets a short explanation and a walk-through of typical scenarios, not just a card. The app can be used on top of any other to close the blind spots before the exam.
features: Separate blocks on junior driver and probationary period restrictions
Fines and consequences of violations with concrete-situation walk-throughs
Calculating allowable alcohol content step by step
Hand signals and headlight rules that other apps don't have
A blind-spot checklist before the exam for your chosen state
antiFeatures: Don't duplicate the basic signs and limits that are everywhere already
Don't present a topic as a single card without a scenario walk-through
Don't promise a full exam, this is specifically topping up the weak topics
driving-test-prep-5.monetization: One topic free as a trial, the full set of top-up topics for a one-time purchase around 5 dollars, positioned as a second app alongside the main trainer

driving-test-prep-6.title: Prep in Spanish, written by people, not machine translation
driving-test-prep-6.oneLiner: Questions and explanations in proper Spanish, with wording like the state exam, not a garbled auto-translation
driving-test-prep-6.gap: In many states the exam can be taken in Spanish, and a huge part of the audience preps in it, but apps give either machine translation that loses the meaning of the question, or jump between English and Spanish right inside a test. The person can't tell what's being asked and memorizes nonsense. Nobody has made prep where Spanish isn't an auto-translation of the English base but properly written questions with wording close to how the exam sounds in Spanish.
mechanisms: Prep in Spanish, written by people, not machine translation
The app jumps between English and Spanish in one test
Spanish speakers give thanks when the language is done like a human's
driving-test-prep-6.pitch: An app for the Spanish-speaking audience where Spanish comes first, not glued on by a translator. Questions and explanations are written like a human's, and the terms match how the state exam phrases them in Spanish. The language doesn't jump mid-test. The same trainer is also available in English for those learning both, but the quality of the Spanish is the whole point of the product here.
features: Questions and explanations in living Spanish, not auto-translation
Terms match the Spanish version of the state exam
One language within a test, no jumps to English
Parallel English for those learning both languages
A tag for states where the exam is actually taken in Spanish
antiFeatures: Don't run the English base through a machine translator
Don't mix two languages within one run
Don't leave Spanish as a secondary, forgotten version
driving-test-prep-6.monetization: Free basic access, the full Spanish bank for a one-time purchase around 5 dollars, with card and local payment methods for an audience without linked cards

driving-test-prep-7.title: CDL by specific endorsement, not a general FMCSA pool
driving-test-prep-7.oneLiner: Separate banks for air brakes, hazmat, passenger, doubles, and triples per your state's manual, with no unrelated topics
driving-test-prep-7.gap: Truck drivers take separate tests for each endorsement: air brakes, combination, hazmat, passenger, tanker, doubles and triples, school bus. Apps drill general knowledge decently, but endorsement coverage is patchy, and questions often come from the general federal manual and ignore the state manual. The person preps for hazmat or passenger and sees half of it unfamiliar on the exam. Nobody has made a trainer where each endorsement is a separate verified bank per the right state's manual.
mechanisms: CDL by specific endorsement, not a general FMCSA pool
Endorsements like hazmat and passenger are covered worse than general knowledge
Breaking down a specific endorsement with part images is praised
driving-test-prep-7.pitch: A CDL trainer built not as a general pile but as a set of separate banks for each test: general knowledge, air brakes, combination, hazmat, passenger, tanker, doubles and triples, school bus. Each bank is verified against the chosen state's manual, not just the federal one. The person takes exactly the endorsement they're testing for and preps without unrelated topics. For complex assemblies like air brakes there are part images.
features: A separate verified bank for each endorsement
Checked against a specific state's manual, not just the federal one
Part images for air brakes and combination
Pick only the tests you need without forcing general knowledge
A pre-exam run-through on one chosen endorsement
antiFeatures: Don't mix in the general federal pool when a state is selected
Don't force you through general knowledge to reach an endorsement
Don't leave hazmat and passenger with patchy coverage
driving-test-prep-7.monetization: One endorsement free as a trial, each additional bank for a one-time purchase around 6 dollars or all at once as a bundle around 15 dollars, betting on the working driver for whom passing is access to a paycheck

driving-test-prep-8.title: Progress that doesn't reset when you leave
driving-test-prep-8.oneLiner: You can interrupt practice and come back to the same spot, with no loss of results on close or login
driving-test-prep-8.gap: People prep in snatches: in a line, at work, on the road. But apps lose progress on close, wipe results on account login, and don't let you pause a long run of questions to return to the same spot. A person goes through dozens of questions, steps away for a minute, and starts from scratch. This breaks the very habit of studying a little at a time. Nobody has bet on saving state locally and instantly, with any run pausable and resumable.
mechanisms: Progress that doesn't reset when you leave
Account login zeroes out what you've done back to the first lesson
Being able to go back and redo what you've covered is valued
driving-test-prep-8.pitch: A trainer for studying in snatches, where progress isn't lost under any conditions. Any run can be interrupted mid-way and resumed on the exact same question. State is stored on the device and saved instantly, account login zeroes out nothing and only syncs. The point is for the person to study for five minutes between things and accumulate results, not start over every time.
features: Instant local saving after each answer
Pause and return to the same question in a long run
Account login syncs but doesn't zero out progress
History of what's covered and weak topics with no reset on update
Works offline, so you can study on the road and without a network
antiFeatures: Don't store progress only on the server, so login can't erase it
Don't force starting a lesson over after leaving
Don't reset stats when the app updates
driving-test-prep-8.monetization: Practice with progress saving free, cross-device sync and expanded stats for a one-time purchase around 4 dollars, no subscription

weight-tracker-1.title: A smoothed weight trend without daily swings
weight-tracker-1.oneLiner: Shows a trend line, not jumps of a pound or two either way
weight-tracker-1.gap: People weigh in every day and see jumps of a couple of pounds from water and salt, and they quit because of it. For those who reach the idea of a trend it genuinely helps them stick with it for years, but most apps either show raw dots or collapse everything into monthly averages and lose the detail. Nobody honestly explains that yesterday's gain is water, or draws a calm moving average next to a date prediction.
mechanisms: A smoothed weight trend without daily swings
Daily weigh-ins scare people with water swings
They want a goal-date prediction, not a bare line
weight-tracker-1.pitch: A tracker that takes your daily weigh-ins and draws not a jagged sawtooth but a calm trend line from a moving average. Every morning you enter a number, and the app tells you one of two things: the trend is going down, or that's just water. The goal-date prediction is recalculated from the slope of the trend, not from the last random point. The single aim: remove the anxiety of daily swings and let you see the real movement.
features: A moving average over the raw dots, with the slope labeled as a number
A tag for each day: real trend or water fluctuation
A goal-date prediction based on the trend slope
View ranges from a week to the entire history on one screen
One input field in the morning, nothing extra
Export of the trend line as an image and CSV
antiFeatures: No meal plans and no calorie counting
Doesn't nag with notifications for a missed weigh-in
No coach and no chats
weight-tracker-1.monetization: Free input and a basic chart, a one-time Pro purchase at 499 rubles for the goal-date prediction, long ranges and export. A yearly plan won't hold: in reviews people are angry precisely at subscriptions for what should be simple.

weight-tracker-2.title: A GLP-1 diary: shot, dose and weight in one place
weight-tracker-2.oneLiner: Logs injections, injection sites, side effects and dose changes next to weight
weight-tracker-2.gap: People on GLP-1 right now glue several apps together: one for shots, another for weight, a third for protein and water. When the doctor changes the dose or moves them to an oral form, the reminders slip and show an overdue that isn't there. After a shot they let you mark only one side effect, though there are usually several. Nobody has built a calm diary where the shot, injection site, dose, a set of side effects and weight sit side by side and survive a change in the treatment plan.
mechanisms: A GLP-1 diary: shot, dose and weight in one place
A dose or oral-form change breaks the reminders
They let you mark only one side effect after a shot
weight-tracker-2.pitch: A diary for people on GLP-1. You mark the shot, injection site and dose, set several side effects at once, and see the weight line across the whole course right next to it. A dose change or a move to an oral form is a separate event in the history, not a broken reminder. Everything in one place, so you don't hop between three apps and lose the picture.
features: A shot log with rotation of injection sites
A dose- and form-change event without resetting reminders
Several side effects on one day with a note
The weight line and protein with water next to the shots
A next-shot reminder tied to your regimen
Export of the history to show a doctor
antiFeatures: No medical advice and no dose selection
Doesn't lock the basic log behind a payment
No selling of supplements and powders
weight-tracker-2.monetization: The shot and weight log is free forever. Pro at 399 rubles a month or 2490 rubles a year for extended side-effect analytics, multiple drugs and export for a doctor. The key: don't hide the act of logging a shot itself behind a payment, that's what catches anger in Glowise reviews.

weight-tracker-3.title: A weight tracker without shame or judging avatars
weight-tracker-3.oneLiner: Numbers and a chart with no fat avatars and no passive aggression
weight-tracker-3.gap: Plenty of trackers draw a fat avatar that swells as you gain weight and send passive-aggressive reminders in the spirit of your mother. For people with a complicated relationship with their body this is a blow to motivation, and they flat out write that they quit because of it. Meanwhile many care about privacy: a passcode on entry and the option not to see the big number right away when they open the app. A calm, respectful tracker without judgment barely exists.
mechanisms: A weight tracker without shame or judging avatars
Passive-aggressive notifications push people away
They want privacy: a passcode and hiding the number
weight-tracker-3.pitch: A weight tracker that treats you like an adult. No avatars that get fatter, no passive aggression in the notifications. Just your numbers, a calm chart and neutral wording. Optionally the number is hidden on open and protected with a passcode, so your weight doesn't jump out when someone else sees the phone. The app's tone stays even whichever way the weight moves.
features: Only numbers and a chart, no body figures
Neutral notifications with no whining or guilt
A passcode or Face ID on entry
A hidden-number mode, weight shown on tap
Gentle wording for both gains and losses in weight
Goal marking without a countdown of pounds
antiFeatures: No avatars and no body images
Doesn't shame or guilt you for missed days
No public leaderboards or comparisons with others
weight-tracker-3.monetization: The core is free. A one-time purchase at 599 rubles for a passcode, a theme and widgets. Deliberately not a subscription: the audience is sensitive to money and to pressure, and a one-time payment is more honest for this topic.

weight-tracker-4.title: Sync with smart scales and Apple Health
weight-tracker-4.oneLiner: Weight from any scale or watch pulls in on its own, no manual entry
weight-tracker-4.gap: People already have smart scales and pour weight into Apple Health, but the trackers either don't read that data or pull only new entries and ignore the accumulated history. Sync keeps dropping after a phone swap or an update, even in paid versions. Support is limited to five scale models from a list. What's needed is a tracker that simply reads Health as the source of truth and survives moves.
mechanisms: Sync with smart scales and Apple Health
Sync breaks after a phone or app update
They want to pull old history from Health, not just new
weight-tracker-4.pitch: A tracker that doesn't make you enter weight by hand if you have a smart scale or watch. It reads Apple Health as the single source, including the entire accumulated history, not just the fresh entries. Sync isn't tied to a specific scale brand: anything that writes to Health works. After a phone swap the data is intact, because the source is Health, not a fragile internal database.
features: Reading the entire weight history from Apple Health, not just new points
Two-way sync: a manual entry goes back into Health
Compatibility with any scale that writes to Health
Data recovery after a phone swap from Health
A trend chart over the pulled-in data
A clear sync status, showing when it last updated
antiFeatures: Doesn't keep the only copy of the data inside itself
No manual pairing of every scale model
Doesn't hide sync behind a payment if the data is already in Health
weight-tracker-4.monetization: Sync and the chart are free. Pro at 699 rubles one-time for extended trend analytics, widgets and export. Paying for sync itself isn't allowed: in Monitor Your Weight reviews people are furious that they bought the version and the sync with the scale dropped.

weight-tracker-5.title: Weight history that an update won't erase
weight-tracker-5.oneLiner: Years of records survive an update, a phone swap and an Android → iOS move
weight-tracker-5.gap: The loudest pain of the niche: people track their weight for years, and then an app update or a phone swap wipes it all with no warning. A move from Android to iOS loses the data forever, because the databases aren't connected. Backups and imports often simply don't exist. For someone who weighed in every morning for three years, losing the history is a catastrophe and an instant one-star review. What's needed is a tracker where data safety is the main feature.
mechanisms: Weight history that an update won't erase
An Android → iOS move loses everything forever
An upgrade to a new version doesn't carry data over
weight-tracker-5.pitch: A tracker built around one promise: your weight history won't be lost. Data lives in your cloud and in Apple Health, there is an automatic backup and a manual CSV export at any moment. A move between phones and from Android to iOS goes through the export file rather than being lost. Version updates never wipe the history, and old records are always imported. Years of weigh-ins are safe.
features: Auto-backup to iCloud and writing to Apple Health
One-tap CSV export and import for a move
Cross-platform transfer via a file, including Android
A guarantee that a new version imports old data
History with no time limit on storage
A clear page with the status of the last backup
antiFeatures: Doesn't keep data only in a local database with no copy
Doesn't ship a redesign that erases the history
No forced sign-up just to access your own records
weight-tracker-5.monetization: Input, the chart and local export are free. Cloud backup and multi-device at 990 rubles a year. The subscription's value is honest: people have already lost years of data and are ready to pay precisely for safety, not to see their weight at all.

weight-tracker-6.title: A progress photo diary with honest comparison
weight-tracker-6.oneLiner: Before-and-after photos in one frame, the same angle and scale
weight-tracker-6.gap: Before-and-after photos motivate people more strongly than numbers, but existing apps ruin the main thing: the comparison. One photo is zoomed in, another zoomed out, thick borders between them, and it's impossible to see the real difference. Sometimes the photos simply go black after an update. Meanwhile body shots are intimate and need a passcode, which isn't everywhere. What's needed is a photo diary where the silhouette lines up to the same angle and scale, and the gallery is under lock.
mechanisms: A progress photo diary with honest comparison
The comparison lies: different zoom and thick borders
Photos and privacy matter together, a lock is needed
weight-tracker-6.pitch: A body photo diary built for honest comparison. When shooting, a semi-transparent outline of the previous photo appears, so you can stand at the same angle and scale. Before and after shots are placed side by side without different zoom and without thick borders, and the difference is visible at once. The whole gallery is behind a passcode or Face ID, because these are body shots. The weight line sits next to it, so photos and numbers line up by date.
features: An outline of the previous shot while shooting, for the same angle
Before-and-after comparison without different scale and borders
Several angles: front, side, back
A passcode and Face ID on the gallery
Tying a photo to a date and weight
Building a progress collage for yourself
antiFeatures: No mandatory upload of photos to a shared feed
Doesn't store shots without passcode protection
No beauty filters that distort the real difference
weight-tracker-6.monetization: A couple of angles and basic comparison are free. Pro at 799 rubles one-time for all angles, collages and encrypted cloud backup. A one-time purchase fits better than a subscription: body photos are personal, and trust matters more than a recurring charge.

weight-tracker-7.title: An all-time weight chart, not a 30-day window
weight-tracker-7.oneLiner: The path is visible from the very start, not the last seven or thirty days
weight-tracker-7.gap: A very common complaint: the app shows only the last seven or thirty days and won't let you see the whole path from the very start. People flat out say the point of tracking is to see the line from the beginning to today, and without it the app is useless. Others, on the contrary, get stuck at a minimum three-month window and can't view one clean month. Nobody lets you freely change the range from a day to the entire history.
mechanisms: An all-time weight chart, not a 30-day window
You can't pick the window: too narrow or too wide
The total number of weight lost motivates people
weight-tracker-7.pitch: A tracker where the chart can be stretched to any span: a day, a month, a year, all time. The line always starts from your starting weight, so the whole path is visible, not the last thirty days. Front and center is one big number: how much has been lost since the start. The range switches with a pinch, without going into settings. Nothing extra, just an honest picture of progress at any scale.
features: Ranges from a single day to the entire history
The line always from the starting weight
A big number for total weight lost
Scale switching with a pinch right on the chart
Saving the chosen range between sessions
Export of the chart as an image
antiFeatures: Doesn't limit the view to a fixed window
No monthly averaging that hides the detail
Doesn't reset the chosen range on every open
weight-tracker-7.monetization: All ranges and the total number are free, that's the base and hiding it isn't allowed. Pro at 490 rubles one-time for widgets, themes and export. In reviews people flat out write they're ready to pay for an all-time view, but get angry when it's a base feature behind a subscription.

weight-tracker-8.title: A BMI calculator with age, sex and no scare tactics
weight-tracker-8.oneLiner: Honest ranges by age and sex, a separate calculation for teens
weight-tracker-8.gap: BMI calculators en masse compute by a single adult formula and ignore age and sex. For teens that gives wild results: a normal weight is called obesity, and a dangerously low BMI is marked as normal, which directly feeds eating disorders. The labels are harsh and without context. What's needed is a calculator that asks for age and sex, computes teen BMI by percentiles, and delivers the result carefully, without scary wording.
mechanisms: A BMI calculator with age, sex and no scare tactics
Teen BMI is computed on an adult scale, the ranges lie
Harsh labels hit self-esteem and feed EDs
weight-tracker-8.pitch: A BMI calculator that finally accounts for age and sex. For teens it computes by age percentiles rather than an adult scale, so it doesn't call a healthy weight obesity or mark a dangerously low one as normal. The result is delivered calmly, with a range and a caveat about muscle and build, without harsh labels that hit self-esteem. Precise height input in fractions of an inch and in centimeters.
features: Accounting for age and sex in the calculation
Teen BMI by age percentiles
Gentle delivery of the result with a range and a caveat about muscle
Precise height input in fractional units
A clear explanation that BMI doesn't account for body composition
Saving measurements and a BMI chart over time
antiFeatures: No harsh labels without context
Doesn't give lowered healthy limits that are dangerous with an ED
No aggressive ad pop-ups over the input
weight-tracker-8.monetization: The calculator is free with ads in one unobtrusive spot. A one-time purchase at 299 rubles removes the ads and unlocks the BMI chart over time. Ads in BMI apps enrage people, so the advertising is modest, and removing it is cheap and one-time.
